column1: # namespace-axes.tsv — THE derivation table for OC_NAMESPACE, and the only copy.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# The same namespace→(root, launchd label, tmux socket, tokfile) derivation is
# implemented across SIX FILES / ELEVEN CODE SITES, in three languages, across
# three Go modules that cannot import each other. Count SITES, not files: this
# header said FOUR, the guard said FIVE, and a later revision said SEVEN — all
# wrong. bin/install.sh carries five sites on its own, including the ocwarden
# label, which is the one this ticket is about and the one that was missing from
# every list. cli/ocagent/config.go was missing for a different reason: it was
# listed as a non-guarded AXIS rather than as a derivation site, and it had no
# namespace in it at all. The FILE number itself has now been wrong four times,
# which is the argument in this header's own first line: count SITES.
#   cli/ocagent/config.go         fallbackAgentsHome (agents-home fallback root)
#   cli/ocwarden/namespace.go     wardenLabelFor / officraftRootFor /
#                                 tmuxSocketFor / tokfileFor
#   server/ocserverd/onboarding.go  wardenLaunchdLabel / officraftRootPath /
#                                 wardenTokfilePath
#   bin/install.sh                NS_DOT / NS_DASH on the install path, and
#                                 ns_dot / ns_dash on the uninstall path — the
#                                 latter for BOTH the serve label AND the
#                                 ocwarden label (5 sites total)
#   bin/ocserver                  the same, on the from-source install path
#   e2e_test/lib/oc_lifecycle.sh  harness-side root derivation, deliberately
#                                 unguarded (see namespace-mirror-guard.sh)
# The authoritative, always-current list of what IS and IS NOT machine-checked
# lives in bin/tests/namespace-mirror-guard.sh's header. Do not treat this comment
# as the coverage claim.
# Those copies are HAND-TRANSCRIBED MIRRORS. The server derives a label to decide
# "does this host already carry a warden?"; the warden derives a label to decide
# which job to bootstrap and boot out. If the two ever disagree by one character,
# the server concludes there is no warden here and installs a second one over the
# live job — the exact three-times-repeated accident this ticket exists for. The
# ticket calls this the single most fragile line in the whole case, and until
# this file there was nothing but a `// keep them in sync` comment holding it.
# HOW IT IS ENFORCED
# Every implementation is tested against THIS TABLE, not against its neighbour.
# Change one side and only that side goes red — which is what makes the failure
# say WHICH copy drifted instead of merely that two copies differ:
#   cli/ocagent/namespace_mirror_test.go        (go test ./cli/ocagent/)
#   cli/ocwarden/namespace_mirror_test.go       (go test ./cli/ocwarden/)
#   server/ocserverd/onboarding_mirror_test.go  (go test ./server/ocserverd/)
#   bin/tests/namespace-mirror-guard.sh         (the two bash copies + charset)
# The table is data, deliberately: adding a namespace case must not require
# touching four implementations' test code.
# FORMAT (tab-separated; '#' comments and blank lines ignored)
#   namespace <TAB> root_suffix <TAB> label <TAB> tmux_socket
# The literal token <empty> means the empty string — a bare empty field between
# two tabs is too easy for an editor, a shell, or a careless reader to eat, and
# the empty namespace is precisely the row whose exactness matters most.
# root_suffix is appended to "$HOME/.officraft" — EMPTY for the main instance,
# which is the property that makes the empty namespace byte-identical to the
# historical literal. The tokfile is always <root>/warden/exec-warden.tok and is
# derived, not listed, so it cannot disagree with root.
# CHARSET (all FIVE copies must carry this exact regex source — cli/ocwarden,
# cli/ocagent, server/ocserverd/config.go, bin/install.sh, bin/ocserver):
# charset
<empty>
